title: Integrative multi-omics identifies MSR1 as a programmed cell death and extracellular matrix hub gene in osteoarthritis with hesperidin targeting potential.
authors: Bao, Jinquan; Wu, Lingling; Zhao, Wenqiang; Li, Bo; Li, Zilong; Bai, Zhigang; Ma, Penglei; Gao, Bo; Qiao, Chenggang
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多组学分析鉴定骨关节炎中MSR1基因，虽涉及转录因子结合位点预测（JASPAR/FIMO）和分子对接，但核心是疾病基因表达与免疫调控，非蛋白质-DNA互作机制研究，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease with complex molecular mechanisms. There is an interplay between programmed cell death (PCD) and extracellular matrix (ECM) in inflammatory diseases. This study aimed to identify a key PCD/ECM-related gene involved in OA pathogenesis through multi-omics analysis. METHODS: RNA-seq data of OA synovial tissue from the GEO databases were analyzed. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), differential expression analysis, cross analysis, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network were used to identify key PCD/ECM-related genes in OA. Regulatory networks were predicted using miRDB, TargetScan, and miRWalk databases, and transcription factor binding was analyzed using JASPAR and FIMO. The role of MSR1 in OA progression was investigated by establishing an IL-1beta-induced in vitro OA cell model. RESULTS: We identified 517 genes associated with OA that were enriched in immune and developmental pathways. Differential expression analysis and cross-analysis revealed 24 OA-associated PCD- and ECM-related genes. MSR1 was identified as the key candidate via PPI network analysis. In both the training and validation sets, MSR1 expression was higher in OA samples than in healthy samples, with an AUC value greater than 0.7. MSR1 expression was positively correlated with key immune populations and microenvironment scores, suggesting a role for MSR1 in OA pathogenesis through immune modulation. In addition, molecular docking identified hesperidin as a high-affinity MSR1-binding compound with favorable interaction stability. In vitro experiments demonstrated that MSR1 was upregulated in IL-1beta-induced OA-like chondrocytes and promoted apoptosis, extracellular matrix degradation, and NF-kappaB pathway activation. CONCLUSION: This study highlights PCD/ECM-related gene MSR1 as a central regulator of OA pathogenesis and proposes hesperidin as a potential therapeutic agent. The integrative approach provides a framework for understanding OA mechanisms and drug discovery.
abstract_zh: 背景：骨关节炎（OA）是一种具有复杂分子机制的退行性关节疾病。在炎症性疾病中，程序性细胞死亡（PCD）与细胞外基质（ECM）之间存在相互作用。本研究旨在通过多组学分析，识别参与OA发病机制的关键PCD/ECM相关基因。方法：分析了来自GEO数据库中OA滑膜组织的RNA-seq数据。采用加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA）、差异表达分析、交叉分析及蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络，以识别OA中的关键PCD/ECM相关基因。利用miRDB、TargetScan和miRWalk数据库预测调控网络，并使用JASPAR和FIMO分析转录因子结合。通过建立IL-1β诱导的体外OA细胞模型，研究了MSR1在OA进展中的作用。结果：我们识别出517个与OA相关的基因，这些基因富集于免疫和发育通路。差异表达分析和交叉分析揭示了24个与OA相关的PCD和ECM相关基因。通过PPI网络分析，MSR1被确定为主要候选基因。在训练集和验证集中，OA样本中MSR1的表达均高于健康样本，AUC值大于0.7。MSR1表达与关键免疫群体及微环境评分呈正相关，提示MSR1通过免疫调节参与OA发病机制。此外，分子对接识别出橙皮苷（hesperidin）为高亲和力MSR1结合化合物，且具有有利的相互作用稳定性。体外实验表明，MSR1在IL-1β诱导的OA样软骨细胞中上调，并促进细胞凋亡、细胞外基质降解及NF-κB通路激活。结论：本研究强调PCD/ECM相关基因MSR1作为OA发病机制的核心调节因子，并提出橙皮苷作为潜在治疗药物。该整合方法为理解OA机制和药物发现提供了框架。
